title: Compact perfect generator on a qcqs algebraic space
statement: Work in the fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For an algebraic space $Z$ over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], use its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Z$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory of objects whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$; quasi-compact means every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated means its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. A perfect object is one locally isomorphic to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules. There exists a perfect object $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ which is compact [def-pc-compact-object]: for every small family $(E_i)$ in this category the canonical map $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(P,E_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,\bigoplus_iE_i)$ is bijective. Moreover, for every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, one has $E\simeq0$ if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(P[n],E)=0$ for every integer $n$.

source.place: Tag 09IY, theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh; compactness of its perfect generator by Tag 09M8, proposition-compact-is-perfect.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-weak-generator] to the given scheme $S$ and qcqs algebraic space $X$. Its small etale structure sheaf, module category, quasi-coherent subcategory and notion of perfect object are exactly those in the statement. Obtain a perfect $P\in C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ with $E\simeq0$ if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(P[n],E)=0$ for every integer $n$, for all $E\in C_X$. Keep this same $P$ in the remaining steps.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-objects-compact] to this perfect object $P$. Both its hypotheses on $X$ (quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness) are assumptions of the item. It asserts compactness in $C_X$, and explicitly gives the bijectivity of the canonical Hom-to-coproduct map for every family in the chosen indexing universe. No compactness in the whole ambient $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is asserted or needed.

Since $C_X$ is a full subcategory, its Hom groups between its objects are the ambient derived-category Hom groups. Thus the compactness formula of step 2 is exactly the formula in the item, and the vanishing criterion of step 1 is exactly its final equivalence. The same object $P$ therefore satisfies all the required clauses.

lean.statement: theorem exists_compact_perfect_generator {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.SmallModules] (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) : ∃ (hcoprod : HasCoproducts.{u} X.DerivedQCoh) (P : X.DerivedQCoh), SheafOfModules.IsPerfectOnRingedSiteOfUniverses.{u, u, u, w} X.smallStructureSheaf P.obj ∧ @IsCompactObject.{u} X.DerivedQCoh _ _ hcoprod P ∧ ∀ E : X.DerivedQCoh, IsZero E.obj ↔ ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (P.obj⟦n⟧ ⟶ E.obj)
lean.note: Uses the existing equivalent small affine ringed model and general local strict-perfect predicate. Absolute quasi-separatedness is expressed by Stacks 0AHR affine-pair fibre products, without assuming the base scheme quasi-separated. The conclusion includes existence of small coproducts, so compactness introduces no extra hypothesis. No stage-1 split is changed.
